title: Egress router: customer-managed storage integration with CMEK + resilient uploads
creator: Priya Patel
description: Build an egress router service for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments that can deliver audit logs to customer-managed storage (cloud object stores and on-prem targets) while supporting customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK), resumable and integrity-verified uploads, and operator controls. This ticket covers the core integration adapter framework, credential lifecycle/handshake patterns, and runtime safety controls that make customer storage options usable in regulated environments.
acceptance_criteria: Egress router can upload audit bundles to S3-compatible endpoints (AWS S3, MinIO) with multipart resume and SHA256 integrity checks
Support for GCS and Azure Blob using storage-adapter interface with consistent metadata and retention headers
Option to use customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) for supported providers with documented handshake flow and key rotation procedure
Handshake protocol for VPC/private deployments that never exposes long-lived customer secrets to Redwood control plane
Backpressure and retry policy ensures no unbounded memory growth during slow/blocked egress targets; test coverage for transient network failures
Admin console shows per-tenant egress status, last successful upload, and actionable operator errors for remediation
proposed_design: Introduce an extensible 'storage-adapter' interface in the egress-router service. Adapters implement: initiate_upload(bundle_metadata) -> upload_handle, upload_chunk(handle, bytes, offset), finalize_upload(handle, metadata), and verify_proof(handle) methods.

Adapters present two modes: signed-upload (pre-signed URLs + client multipart) and server-upload (egress-router streams to provider). Private deployments can opt for server-upload to avoid client credentials in control plane.

Credential model: ephemeral capability tokens issued by a local operator agent in private deployment mode. For cloud-managed targets, we support either customer-managed IAM roles (IRSA/assume-role) or provided static creds that are stored encrypted with HSM/KMS using customer keys (CMEK where supported).

CMEK integration: for providers that support CMEK (GCS, AWS S3 with KMS envelope), the adapter will store only the CMEK key id and perform server-side encryption calls. For on-prem object stores that don't support CMEK, we provide client-side encryption option with envelope keys stored in the customer's KMS when available.

Resiliency: all uploads are resumable using multipart semantics or a custom chunking protocol with manifest and SHA256 checks for each chunk. Egress-router persists minimal upload state to local ephemeral storage with TTL and operator-visible traces.

Security controls: RBAC v2 hooks to gate who can configure egress targets; SSO/SAML admin flows required for creating tenant-level storage configs; audit events emitted for create/update/delete of egress targets with originator identity and SAML assertion id.

Operator UX: Console pages to create storage connectors with test-upload button, view recent upload traces, and trigger manual replays for failed bundles. CLI tooling for airgapped/on-prem to inject credentials and run handshake tests.

Observability: metric counters (uploads_started, uploads_success, uploads_retry, uploads_failed), per-tenant upload latency histograms, and span annotations with chunk-level checksums. Logs redact credentials and expose only non-sensitive diagnostic fields.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customer keys accidentally exfiltrated if long-lived creds are stored in control plane. Mitigation: default to ephemeral capability tokens + operator local agent for private deployments; encrypt any stored secrets with customer-managed KMS and restrict admin UI to RBAC v2 roles.

Risk: Large backlog of audit bundles when target storage is slow causing disk pressure. Mitigation: bounded local queue with configurable retention policies, backpressure to upstream collector, and an operator alert when queue exceeds threshold.

Risk: Incompatible provider behaviors (S3 vs GCS vs Azure) cause subtle metadata/lifecycle differences. Mitigation: normalize metadata at the adapter layer and document provider-specific caveats; add e2e tests across each provider.

Risk: Replay of partially uploaded bundles might produce duplicate events at customer side. Mitigation: include idempotency keys and manifest checks; make replay opt-in and log all replay actions in audit logs.

Risk: CMEK key rotation invalidates previous server-side encryption. Mitigation: document rotation window, support re-encrypt/re-upload flows via operator tools, and surface warnings when rotated keys are detected during upload attempts.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (lab): implement storage-adapter interface + S3-compatible adapter with multipart resume and tests. Deploy to an isolated internal private deployment for soak (2 weeks).

Phase 2 (beta): add GCS and Azure adapters, CMEK handshake flows, and console UX for creating connectors. Invite 2 pilot customers to test with real buckets. Collect feedback and add provider-specific fixes.
Phase 3 (GA): RBAC v2 gating, SSO/SAML admin flows integration, and hardened retry policies. Provide migration docs and runbook for customer support.
qa_and_testing: Unit tests for adapter interface and chunk verification logic
Integration tests against local MinIO, AWS S3 (test account), GCS test bucket, and Azure Blob emulator
Fault-injection tests that simulate network partitions and high-latency endpoints, verifying bounded memory and retry behavior
Security review focusing on secret handling, KMS interactions, and SSO assertion propagation
E2E test that verifies admin-configured connector can successfully upload a 1GB compressed audit bundle and be replayed without data corruption
